Acquisition / Lead economics

Media cost per qualified lead (CPQL)

Media spend per unique attributed lead that meets your documented qualification rules. Those rules might cover company fit, geography, need, budget, or accepted sales intent; qualification is agreed for each client.

Level 4Inspect the detail

Media spend per unique attributed lead that meets your documented qualification rules. Those rules might cover company fit, geography, need, budget, or accepted sales intent; qualification is agreed for each client.

currency / qualified lead

How we use it

Helps separate lead volume from sales readiness. We connect enrichment, scoring, and sales acceptance to reveal where campaign targeting or qualification rules need improvement.

Transparent calculationAttributed media spend ÷ unique attributed leads meeting the agreed qualification criteria
media spend6,000
qualified leads30

6,000 ÷ 30 = 200 currency units per qualified lead.

Illustrative calculation. Not a client result or a universal benchmark.

Break the result down

  • Campaign and lead source
  • Qualification segment
  • Market and offer

Questions we investigate

  • Is the qualification rule applied consistently?
  • Which sources create qualified leads efficiently?
  • Are delayed reviews suppressing qualified counts?

Actions the evidence supports

  • Calibrate shared qualification criteria.
  • Improve routing and review ownership.
  • Allocate experiments using downstream outcomes.

Reporting contract

Ownership & cadence

Marketing and sales operations leads
Weekly after qualification windows mature.

Required data

  • Attributed campaign spend
  • Deduplicated qualified lead cohort
  • Qualification rules and review timestamps

Read the measure with context

Zero qualified leads makes CPQL undefined. Changing qualification criteria changes the metric. Allow enough time for a lead cohort to mature. Media-only CPQL excludes labor, enrichment, and software costs; report an all-in version separately when needed.
